note: Part B (drawing) is not transcribed: no model answer exists.

questions.text: A painter mixes white and black paints to create different shades in two different buckets. He prepares 10 kg in one bucket with 20% black paint in it. He then prepares 20 kg of another shade in the second bucket with 20% black paint in it. He pours the second bucket into the first one. What is the percentage of black paint in the mixture?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The first bucket has 2 kg of black in 10 kg and the second has 4 kg of black in 20 kg. Together that is 6 kg of black in 30 kg, which is 20%. Mixing two shades with the same percentage of black always keeps that percentage.

questions.text:
"Betty bought some butter but the butter was too bitter, so she put a little gummy to make the bitter butter yummy."

In the above sentence, if you replace every letter 't' with letter 'b', what is the total number of instances in which the same letter appears at least twice in a word?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: After the change the words are: Bebby, boughb, some, bubber, bub, bhe, bubber, was, boo, bibber, so, she, pub, a, libble, gummy, bo, make, bhe, bibber, bubber, yummy. Count each letter that repeats inside a word once: Bebby (b), boughb (b), bubber (b), bub (b), bubber (b), boo (o), bibber (b), libble (l and b, so 2), gummy (m), bibber (b), bubber (b), yummy (m and y, so 2). That gives 1+1+1+1+1+1+1+2+1+1+1+2 = 14.

questions.text: In the 3 × 3 square on the left, the numbers from 1 to 9 have been filled so that the sum in each row / column / diagonal adds up to 15. If the same exercise is to be carried out for the 4 × 4 square, using the numbers from 1 to 16, what will be the sum of the numbers in each row / column / diagonal?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The numbers 1 to 16 add up to 136. The four rows must share this total equally, so each row, column and diagonal adds to 136 divided by 4, which is 34. The figure agrees: the corners 7, 14, 9 and 4 add to 34.

questions.text: 10 people are standing in a circle. Each person is assigned a number as shown in the figure below. The first person (numbered 1) is removed. Thereafter, in the clockwise direction, every third person is removed and this is repeated till only two people are left. What is the sum of the numbers assigned to the two people who are left at the end?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The numbers run 1 to 10 clockwise. Remove 1, then count three people clockwise each time: 4 goes, then 7, then 10, then 5 (counting 2, 3, 5), then 9 (6, 8, 9), then 6 (2, 3, 6), then 3 (8, 2, 3). People 2 and 8 remain, and 2 + 8 = 10.

questions.text: A cube 4 cm x 4 cm x 4 cm has all its corners chamfered as shown in the figure below. On each of its faces it has got a small tetrahedral notch having edges of 1 cm each. What is the sum of the number of vertices and the number of edges in this solid?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Chamfering all 8 corners gives a truncated cube: each corner becomes a triangle, so there are 8 x 3 = 24 vertices and 12 + 8 x 3 = 36 edges. Each tetrahedral notch is a triangle on the face plus one apex inside, adding 4 vertices and 6 edges. Six notches add 24 vertices and 36 edges. So the solid has 48 vertices and 72 edges, and 48 + 72 = 120.

questions.text: With a straight cut you can slice a circular piece of paper into two pieces. A second cut that crosses the first cut will produce a maximum of four pieces. What is the maximum number of pieces that you can get with a total of four straight cuts?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each new cut adds as many pieces as the number of regions it passes through, which is one more than the number of earlier cuts it crosses. So the pieces go 2, 4, 7, 11: the third cut crosses 2 cuts and adds 3, the fourth crosses 3 and adds 4. Four cuts give at most 11 pieces.

questions.text: What is the highest number of occurrences of a shape in the figure shown?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Sort the overlapping outlines by shape and count each family separately: pentagons, rounded four-pointed stars, many-pointed bursts, and sharp stars with different numbers of points. Trace each closed outline once and tick it off, since many shapes overlap and partly hide one another. IIT Bombay's final key gives 9 for the most frequent shape. This is a dense picture, so a careful count can easily land one or two off.

questions.text: Each of the rings in the chain in the given figure has an outer diameter of 5 cm and a cross-sectional diameter of 1 cm. What is the maximum end to end length of the chain in cm?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The chain has 10 rings (5 seen face-on and 5 seen edge-on, alternating). Pulled tight, each ring adds its inner diameter, 5 minus 2 x 1 = 3 cm, and the two end rings add their wire thickness of 1 cm at each end. Length = 10 x 3 + 2 x 1 = 32 cm.

questions.text: If 1 inch = 25 mm = 6 pica and 1 pica = 12 points = 16 pixels, what is 6 points + 2 inches + 3 picas + 8 pixels + 25 mm, represented in pixels?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: 1 pica = 16 pixels, so 1 inch = 6 picas = 96 pixels and 1 point = 16/12 pixels. Then 6 points = 8 px, 2 inches = 192 px, 3 picas = 48 px, 8 pixels = 8 px and 25 mm = 1 inch = 96 px. The total is 8 + 192 + 48 + 8 + 96 = 352 pixels.

questions.text: What number will replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Opposite sectors share a colour. In each pair the larger number is the product of the smaller number, the one before it and the one after it: 3 gives 2 x 3 x 4 = 24, 4 gives 3 x 4 x 5 = 60, 6 gives 5 x 6 x 7 = 210. So 5 gives 4 x 5 x 6 = 120.

questions.text: What three-digit number can be made from the digits 2, 3, 5, and 7, such that no two digits of the three-digit number are the same and the three-digit number is divisible by each of the digits in it?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: A number divisible by both 2 and 5 must end in 0, so 2 and 5 cannot both be used. With 2, 3 and 7 the number must be even and divisible by 7, but 372 and 732 are not. With 3, 5 and 7 it must end in 5: 375 is not divisible by 7, but 735 = 3 x 245 = 5 x 147 = 7 x 105. So the number is 735.

questions.text: 27 cubes of edge 10 cm are arranged to create a larger cube. If the cubes at the eight corners are replaced with spheres of diameter 10 cm, what is the minimum number of cubes that do not touch any of the spheres?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each sphere fits exactly in its corner space and touches the middle of each face it shares with a neighbouring cube. The 12 edge cubes share a face with corner spaces, so they touch spheres. The 6 face-centre cubes and the 1 centre cube only meet the corner spaces along an edge or at a point, which the sphere does not reach. So 6 + 1 = 7 cubes touch no sphere.

questions.text: Some of the shapes in the image K are either flipped or rotated in the image J. What is the number of flipped shapes in image J?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Match each of the 12 squiggles in K with its partner in J, then check whether it can be turned onto its partner or needs a mirror image. Ten of them line up by rotation alone (some are not even rotated). Two need a mirror image: the large S-shaped hook at the top and the curled hook in the middle of K. So 2 shapes are flipped.

questions.text: How many different patterns of pens are present in the given figure?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Group the pens by the pattern on their grip: comb-like teeth, chevrons, slanted stripes, curved stripes, and full spiral stripes with a rounded end. Checking every pen against these groups gives 5 different patterns.

questions.text: Which of the options below can be rearranged to make image Q?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: A rearrangement keeps every piece's shape, size and colour. Image Q is a tangram swan made of seven pieces: a large black triangle, a large green triangle, a medium red triangle, a small red triangle, a small blue triangle, a black square and a black parallelogram. B and D contain exactly these seven pieces, only moved and turned, so both can make Q. A has a medium-sized blue triangle and C a large red triangle, which Q does not have.

questions.text: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which of the states shown below?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The outlines are Gujarat (A), Maharashtra (B), Madhya Pradesh (C) and West Bengal (D). The Tropic of Cancer (about 23.5 degrees N) crosses Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal. Maharashtra lies wholly south of it, so B is wrong.

questions.text: Which of the following is / are TRUE for the strip of paper shown in the image?

options.label: B
options.text: An ant can walk all over the surface of the strip without having to cross an edge.

options.label: C
options.text: A rotating belt that is similar to the strip of paper will have a uniform wear and tear.

options.label: D
options.text: This is an optical illusion that can be created as a 2D image but is not possible in 3D.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The strip is a Mobius strip: a band given a half twist before its ends are joined. It has only one edge and one side, so an ant can cover the whole surface without crossing an edge, and a belt made this way wears evenly on its whole surface. It is easily made from real paper, so it is not an impossible figure. A and D are false.

questions.text: Which of the options is / are CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: The cap of a water bottle is tightened by rotating it in the clockwise direction (as seen from the top).

options.label: B
options.text: To turn on a tap, the tap head is rotated clockwise; to turn it off it is rotated counter-clockwise (as seen from the top).

options.label: C
options.text: To loosen a nut of a car wheel, a spanner is turned counter-clockwise clockwise (from the point of view of the person using the spanner).

options.label: D
options.text: The earth as seen from the North Pole rotates clockwise about its axis.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Standard right-hand threads tighten clockwise and loosen counter-clockwise, so a bottle cap is tightened clockwise (A true) and a wheel nut is loosened counter-clockwise (C true). A tap is opened by turning it counter-clockwise, so B is reversed. Seen from above the North Pole, the earth turns counter-clockwise (west to east), so D is false.

questions.text: In the image below, gear 1 rotates in the direction of the arrow. Which of the statements is / are CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 6 rotate in the same direction.

options.label: B
options.text: 3 and 6 rotate in the opposite direction.

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 4 rotate in the opposite direction.

options.label: D
options.text: 2 and 6 rotate in the same direction.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Gear 1 turns clockwise. Its belt to gear 2 is crossed, so 2 turns counter-clockwise. Meshing gears reverse direction: 3 is clockwise and 4 is counter-clockwise. The open belt from 4 keeps 5 counter-clockwise, and 6, meshing with 5, is clockwise. So 1 and 6 match (A true), 3 and 6 match (B false), 1 and 4 are opposite (C true), 2 and 6 are opposite (D false).

questions.text: Which of the options does NOT / do NOT match the pieces in the jigsaw puzzle shown in image K?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: K is a square cut into four pieces: orange at the top, purple on the right, blue on the left and brown at the bottom. Each piece has one or two straight sides from the square's edge and one jagged edge where it meets the others. B is the orange piece as it stands, and C is the purple piece turned. A has the outline of the blue piece and D the outline of the brown piece, but their jagged edges are different: the point and notch on A and the stepped bump on D are not the shapes cut in K. So A and D do not match.

questions.text: P and Q show two different views of the same solid object. Which of the options represent(s) the top view of the solid object?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: From P and Q the four faces of the pyramid carry, going round one way, a solid cylinder, a half pipe, a box and a hollow tube; so the solid cylinder is opposite the box and the half pipe is opposite the tube. Seen from the top, going anticlockwise, the order must be cylinder, half pipe, box, tube. A and D show this order (D is A turned a quarter turn). B has the same pieces in mirror order, and C has two plain rectangles (two boxes).

questions.text: Which consultant(s) to the Government of India suggested that the metal lota (shown in the given figure) used by many Indians is an appropriate symbol for indigenous design traditions?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Charles and Ray Eames wrote The India Report (1958) for the Government of India, which led to the National Institute of Design, and in it they held up the lota as a model of good design. Walter Gropius and Hannes Meyer were Bauhaus directors and were not the authors of that report.

questions.text: Given below are the silhouettes of two iconic figures in Indian history. Which of the following statements is / are TRUE?

options.label: B
options.text: Both spent time in South Africa

options.label: C
options.text: The birthdays of both are in the same month

options.label: D
options.text: Both dressed in a manner that expressed their ideology

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The silhouettes are Mahatma Gandhi (with staff and spectacles) and Dr B. R. Ambedkar (pointing, holding a book). Both qualified as barristers in London (A true). Only Gandhi lived in South Africa (B false). Gandhi was born on 2 October and Ambedkar on 14 April (C false). Gandhi's khadi dhoti and Ambedkar's western suit were both deliberate statements of their ideas (D true).

questions.text: Centuries ago, a rich man left behind a treasure represented as a red dot, in the schematic drawing below. If the corners of the triangle represent central locations in the states of Bihar, Telangana and Rajasthan, which is / are the state(s) where one could hunt for this treasure?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The dot is at the middle of one side, and the drawing is only schematic, so it can be the midpoint of any side. Halfway between Bihar and Telangana lies Chhattisgarh, halfway between Telangana and Rajasthan lies Madhya Pradesh, and halfway between Bihar and Rajasthan lies Uttar Pradesh. West Bengal and Punjab are not midway between any two of the three.

questions.text: Which of the options has / have been created by using only a single wire?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: A single wire has only two free ends, here the two temple tips. In C the wire runs down one temple, along the bar to the bridge, round the left lens and back, round the right lens and back, and along the other bar to the other temple. In D it runs down one temple, round the left lens, along the top bar, round the right lens and up the other temple. In A and B the temples are joined to the frame by twisted wraps at the hinges, and the frame meets each hinge with three branches, so at least two pieces of wire are needed.

questions.text: Which of the options will replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: From TEA, EAT and ATE: T is two squares, A is one square and E is a tall bar. The code with the question mark is six squares and no bar, so any word of T's and A's whose squares add to 6 fits. TATA = 2+1+2+1, AAAAAA = 6 x 1, TAAT = 2+1+1+2 and TTT = 3 x 2 all give six squares, so all four options are correct.

questions.text: Which of the options has / have shapes that DO NOT match the outlines in figure K?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: Every filled shape in an option should be a copy of one closed outline in K, possibly turned or flipped. Match the shapes one at a time against K's outlines. In A and C every shape fits an outline of K. In B the large feathered curl has a short, blunt tail, unlike the long tapering tail of the curl in K. In D the large hooked shape at the bottom right matches none of K's outlines. So B and D have shapes that do not match K.

questions.text: An object was sharply focused and a photograph was taken using a camera. The photographer wants to blur the background (change the depth of field) in the next photograph. This can be achieved by changing the

options.label: A
options.text: size of opening of the lens (aperture).

options.label: B
options.text: distance of the object from the camera and again focusing.

options.label: C
options.text: shutter speed to change the duration for which light enters the camera.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Depth of field depends on the aperture (a wider opening gives a shallower zone of sharpness), the subject distance (focusing closer makes it shallower) and the focal length (a longer lens makes it shallower). Shutter speed only changes how long light enters, which affects exposure and motion blur but not depth of field, so C is wrong.

questions.text: Which of the options can be generated by revolving the quadrilateral in image K, about its edge?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: K is a right trapezium (a short top, a long bottom, a vertical left side and a slanted right side). Turning it about the left side gives a frustum (D). About the long bottom it gives a cylinder capped by a cone (C). About the short top it gives a cylinder with a conical hollow in one end (B). About the slanted side it gives a cone on one end with a conical hollow in the other (A). Each option is one of these solids.

questions.text: What is the length of the edge of the largest cube that can be placed inside a sphere of radius 10 cm?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The largest cube touches the sphere with all eight corners, so its space diagonal equals the sphere's diameter, 20 cm. A cube of edge a has space diagonal a times root 3, so a = 20 / root 3 cm.

questions.text: What is the total number of triangles in the figure given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Count region by region, using straight sides only. Hat: 3. Neck: 3 on each side, 6. Body front, using the long slanting line, the vertical through the circle and the two diagonals from the left point: 7. Front legs: 3 on each side, 6. Hind legs: the narrow triangle between the leg lines, one beside each outer leg, and one large triangle on each side using the top of the semicircle, 5. Total 3 + 6 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 27.

questions.text: Image K is rotated by an angle of 45 degrees anticlockwise. Which option represents the rotated image?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Two things must both turn. The frame of K has its top-right and bottom-left corners cut flat, so after a 45 degree anticlockwise turn the flat corners sit at the top and bottom of the diamond. The pattern of pieces must also match K turned the same way. B and C carry the correctly turned pattern, but only B has flat top and bottom corners (C's flat corners are at the sides).

questions.text: Which of the options is the correct logo of India Post?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The India Post logo is a red rectangle crossed by three curved yellow lines that sweep out beyond its top left corner. The Hindi name, Bharatiya Dak, sits above the rectangle, lined up with its left edge, and the words India Post sit below it, lined up with its right edge. Only D places both pieces of text this way.

questions.text:
What is the next number in the sequence below?

341, 214, 123, 62, 25, ?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Each term is a cube minus 2: 341 = 7 cubed minus 2, 214 = 6 cubed minus 2, 123 = 5 cubed minus 2, 62 = 4 cubed minus 2, 25 = 3 cubed minus 2. The next is 2 cubed minus 2 = 6.

questions.text: Which option is the odd one out?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: In A, B and D both words read the same backwards (palindromes): WOW, MADAM, CIVIC, ROTATOR, NOON, SAGAS. In C, LEVEL is a palindrome but SOLO is not (it reverses to OLOS).

questions.text: Which option will replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Track the two parts separately. The five black inner pieces turn 15 degrees clockwise at every step. The four outer triangles swing 30 degrees one way and then back again, so in frames 2 and 4 they sit at the corners and in frames 1, 3 and 5 at top, right, bottom and left. The missing frame needs the corner position for the triangles and the inner pieces turned 15 degrees clockwise from frame 1. B has the inner pieces unturned and D has the triangles in the wrong position. A and C both look close, but only C copies the pieces exactly.

questions.text: Phulkari, Chikankari, Sambalpuri and Paithani are weaving traditions from different states of India. Which option lists them in the correct sequence?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Phulkari is the embroidery of Punjab, Chikankari the white embroidery of Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, Sambalpuri the ikat weave of Odisha and Paithani the silk sari of Maharashtra. Only B gives Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, Maharashtra.

questions.text: What is the number of fonts used in the following sentence?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Read the sentence phrase by phrase and mark where the letter shapes change: look at serifs (the small feet on letters), the contrast between thick and thin strokes, letter width and weight. Phrases that look different may still share one typeface, so compare their letters (for example the shapes of a, e and t) before counting a new font. Grouping the phrases this way gives 5 fonts, the answer in IIT Bombay's final key.

questions.text: The _______ government organizes the Hornbill Festival each December, promoting cultural heritage and fostering interaction between tribes. The festival has been named after a ______.
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The Hornbill Festival is held by the Government of Nagaland from 1 to 10 December at Kisama near Kohima. It is named after the hornbill, a bird respected in Naga folklore. Shillong is a city, not a state, and the festival is not held in Chhattisgarh or Manipur.

questions.text: The lost wax process is used for ______________.
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: In lost wax casting a wax model is covered in clay, the wax is melted out and molten metal is poured into the hollow, as in Dhokra and Chola bronzes. Batik uses wax as a dye resist, but it is not the lost wax process; honey and jaggery making do not use it.

questions.text: You need to hang a large rectangular picture frame on a wall in an empty room. To ensure that it is vertical (and not tilted), which of the following will help you hang the picture correctly (not tilted)? (No additional items are to be used other than the ones specified in each of the options)

options.label: A
options.text: A wooden stick, a cutter and a pencil

options.label: B
options.text: A pencil, a compass and a cutter

options.label: C
options.text: A flexible and transparent pipe and a mug of water

options.label: D
options.text: Some card paper, a steel-ruler and a pair of scissors

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: To hang the frame level you need something that responds to gravity. A clear pipe partly filled with water works as a water level: the water stands at the same height at both ends, so you can mark two level points on the wall. The other sets can draw and cut but give no reference for horizontal or vertical.

questions.text: Which of the options is the odd one?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The cobra, the krait and the viper are venomous snakes (three of India's 'big four'). The rat snake is not venomous, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Which of the following options is the odd one?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Electroplating, anodizing and powder coating are surface finishes that add a protective or decorative layer to a part. Drilling is a machining process that removes material to make a hole, so it is the odd one.

questions.text:
What is the next number in the sequence below?

7, 11, 18, 30, 50, ___
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The gaps are 4, 7, 12, 20, and the gaps between those are 3, 5, 8, each the sum of the two before. The next is 5 + 8 = 13, so the next gap is 20 + 13 = 33 and the next number is 50 + 33 = 83.

questions.text: The well-known masterpiece "Mona Lisa" was painted by Leonardo Da Vinci in the 16th Century. Nearly 500 years later another artist made a satirical reference to it; he copied the "Mona Lisa" but painted a moustache on her! Which art movement was this artist associated with?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Marcel Duchamp drew a moustache and goatee on a postcard of the Mona Lisa in 1919 and titled it L.H.O.O.Q. Duchamp was a leading figure of Dada, the anti-art movement that mocked established art. Cubism, Impressionism and Pop Art are other movements.

questions.text: Which of the options matches the fruit and the leaf correctly? (the images are not to scale)
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Leaf 3 is long, narrow and pointed, the typical mango leaf. Leaf 4 is a glossy, dark elliptic leaf like the sapodilla (chikoo). Leaf 2 is a smaller oval leaf with clear parallel veins, as on guava. Leaf 1 is the large broad leathery leaf of the jackfruit. Only B pairs them this way.

questions.text: Which are the rivers numbered from 1 to 4 in the map below?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: River 1 flows out of Himachal Pradesh into Punjab: the Sutlej (the Chenab is further north in Jammu and Kashmir). River 2 runs south past Delhi, west of and parallel to the Ganga: the Yamuna. River 3 crosses the middle of the Deccan to the Bay of Bengal: the Godavari. River 4 is the southernmost, through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu: the Cauvery.

questions.text: Which of the sequences in the options will result in the right pattern for a running man?

options.label: A
options.text: K Q J G Y F H

options.label: B
options.text: K G J Q Y F H

options.label: C
options.text: K F Q G Y J H

options.label: D
options.text: K F Q J Y G H

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: K and H are the same full-stride pose, so the frames between must close the legs and open them again. After the stride the back leg lifts (G), the back foot kicks up as the front leg takes the weight (J), the legs pass each other (Q), the other leg starts to reach forward (Y), the stride opens (F) and returns to full stride (H). That is K G J Q Y F H.

questions.text: Which of the following is the hardest wood?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Hardness of wood is measured by how much force it takes to press a steel ball into it (the Janka test). Indian rosewood is the densest and hardest of these four woods, which is why it is used for fine furniture and carving that must take wear. Thorny acacia (babul) is hard too, but less so than rosewood. Teak is prized for durability and resistance to water rather than hardness, and mango wood is comparatively soft.

questions.text: Hex codes are used to specify colours on the computer. What colour is the Hex Code CCCCCC?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Each pair of hex digits is one of red, green and blue on a scale from 00 to FF (0 to 255). CC is 204, which is 80% of 255, and equal red, green and blue give a grey. So CCCCCC is a light grey, 80% of the way to white. FFFFFF would be white and 000000 black.

questions.text: Which is the correct representation in the options, if the image K shown below is flipped about the vertical axis (shown on the right side of K)?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Flipping about a vertical axis reverses the order of the tiles in each row and mirrors every tile. The top row of three 2-like tiles becomes three S-like tiles. The middle row (two meander tiles then a 2-like tile) becomes an S-like tile followed by the two meanders, each mirrored. The bottom row (S-like, 2-like, meander) becomes mirrored meander, S-like, 2-like. Only D shows this.

questions.text: Shapes are cut out from two Black Discs, Disc-X and Disc-Y as given below. Identify the correct image, when Disc-Y is kept on top of Disc-X and rotated 60 degrees anti-clockwise.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: With one disc on the other, light passes only where both discs are cut, so the visible hole is the overlap of the star in X and the turned three-armed cut in Y. Turning Y 60 degrees anticlockwise lines its arms up with three of the star's points, and the overlap is the shape in B.

questions.text: In the cursed land of Weirdisthan, strength of animals was disproportionately distributed. Horse has half the strength of a Dog and four times the strength of an Elephant. Monkey has three times the strength of a Rhino. Elephant has half the strength of a Rhino. One Dog was becoming a danger for other animals and they decided to assign a team of animal soldiers to overpower him. Which team of soldiers managed to overpower the dog?

options.label: B
options.text: One Rhino, One Horse and One Elephant

questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Let an elephant have strength 1. A horse is 4, a dog is 8, a rhino is 2 and a monkey is 6. Rhino plus monkey is 8 (only equal), rhino plus horse plus elephant is 7 (weaker), two horses are 8 (equal), and horse plus monkey is 10. Only C is stronger than the dog.

questions.text: A clock is displaced horizontally at a uniform rate along the direction shown. If the tip of the hour hand is traced from 2 AM to 9 AM, which option shows the correct tracing pattern?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: While the clock slides right, the height of the hour hand's tip follows the hand: at 2 it is half a hand-length above the centre, at 6 it is a full length below, and at 9 it is level with the centre. So the trace starts fairly high, dips to its lowest point a little past the middle (at 6, four of the seven hours), then rises to end below its starting height. Only A has this shape.

questions.text: Which of the options shows the word "TRANSFORM" as it would appear after it is reflected horizontally along AXIS 1 and then vertically along AXIS 2, as indicated in the figure below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Reflecting in the horizontal axis turns the word upside down, and reflecting that in the vertical axis reverses it left to right. Together the two reflections are a half turn, so the word reads MROFSNART with every letter upside down. A is only flipped upside down, C is only mirrored, and D has an R in a different typeface; B is the exact half turn.

questions.text: The shape L is extruded along Z-axis to form a solid as shown in the figure. How many shapes in the Set K will have more than 8 surfaces when extruded along Z-axis?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: An extruded solid has a top, a bottom and one side surface for each edge of the outline (a curved edge gives one curved surface). The L has 6 edges, so 8 surfaces. The plus has 12 edges (14 surfaces), the flat-bottomed V has 7 edges (9 surfaces) and the K-like shape has about 10 edges including its round end (12 surfaces), so these three have more than 8. The bar with a slanted end has 4 edges (6 surfaces) and the two quarter circles have 6 edges (8 surfaces).

questions.text: Residents of planet Earthella are planning to abandon it and fly to planet Marsella because of an acute water crisis. They may choose any of the flight paths connecting Earthella to Marsella through a set of intermediate refuelling stations. How many unique flight paths be charted out if paths cannot retrace any segment that they have already traversed or revisit any station (including Earthella)?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Name the stations top-left (T), top-right (U), centre (C), bottom-left (B) and bottom-right (D). The links are E-T, E-C, E-B, T-U, T-C, U-C, U-M, C-B, C-D, C-M, B-D and D-M. Listing every route from E to M that never repeats a station, starting with E-T, then E-C, then E-B, gives 8 + 5 + 8 = 21 paths.
